title: The Truth About Samsung's Earnings: What They Won't Tell You
speaker: Ricky Gutierrez

macro_themes.view: Pentagon is preparing for possible renewed combat with Iran; Middle East uncertainty pushes oil higher (Brent above $101), which feeds inflation ahead of CPI.
Markets at all-time highs while bond yields are 'through the roof' and the Fed may hike again in 2026; don't be leveraged at overbought levels.
Memory makers like Samsung are printing money from AI capex, but more supply (Toshiba) could shrink margins in a cyclical business.
Leveraged ETFs are not investment vehicles; Korean retail lost $1.7B in three months on them.

calls.condition: Waiting to buy if Nasdaq and S&P pull back
calls.reason: Nasdaq was selling off after Samsung earnings; markets overbought with high yields and possible Fed hikes; cites Jim Paulsen's view of a possible 15% S&P drop in 3-5 months.
calls.quote: if NASDAQ and S&P 500 begin to pull on back, I believe that everything will fall with it and I would rather wait for that …

calls.condition: Invest without leverage; margins at risk if supply (Toshiba) rises
calls.reason: Memory makers are highly profitable beneficiaries of hyperscaler AI spending, but the stock is volatile (1,250 to 700 drawdown) and cyclical.
calls.quote: Again, there's nothing wrong with investing in Micron. There's everything wrong when using leverage ETFs

calls.reason: Escalating Iran tensions; Middle East uncertainty lifts oil, which would push CPI higher.
calls.quote: anytime that there's uncertainty in the Middle East, oil prices will trade higher.
